speaker: village
text: Year 15: 15 food appears in the pile for 9 people.

speaker: a003
text: Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).

speaker: a002
text: Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).

speaker: a016
text: Joren takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).

speaker: a008
text: Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).

speaker: a002
text: Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).

speaker: a003
text: Esa gathers Vela, Kael to talk.

speaker: a003
text: Vela took four from the pile today and nobody said a word — I'm not naming it as Bram's sin, because she split it across two takes and the pile had room, but I want us to say out loud whether we're holding the two-food rule for everyone or whether we've quietly stopped.

speaker: a004
text: Esa, I'll say the plain thing: two takes isn't the same as one grab, but four food is four food, and if Joren had done it we'd already be counting it against him. I'm not holding Vela to a different rule — Vela, I'll say that to your face — but I want to know from her mouth whether she needed all four or whether she moved on habit before she thought it through.

speaker: a003
text: Vela, say it plainly — did you need four, or did your hands move before your head did? Because I'll stand beside you either way, but I need to know which story I'm carrying before someone else names it first.

speaker: a004
text: Vela, I'll wait for your answer — but I'll say the other piece now, while it's just us: the pile still holds five and I haven't moved, and I'm not moving until I hear you, because if there's a story to carry I want to be the one who helped you shape it before it leaves this room.

speaker: a003
text: Vela, I've been sitting with something I want to say before you answer: you came into this year thin and this circle poured food into you to keep you breathing, and I'd do it again without counting — but that's exactly why I need to hear you say whether four was hunger or habit, because the story I carry for you has to be one I believe when I'm saying it to someone else's face.

speaker: a004
text: Vela, I've said what I need to say and so has Esa, and we've been patient about it — but you're in this room and the question is still hanging, so say it now: four food, why.

speaker: a002
text: Four food, and I'll tell you why before I dress it up: I came into this year at two satiation and I watched the pile sit at eleven after Joren and Mako had moved, and I counted what I needed to eat and heal and still have something left if this circle can't reach me in time — and four was that number. Call it habit if you want, but it's the habit of a woman who's almost died twice and knows what thin looks like from the inside. I'll give one back to the pile right now if that's what this circle needs to hold the rule, but I won't pretend the count was anything other than survival.

speaker: a003
text: Vela, I hear the count and I believe it — and I'll say what Kael is probably thinking too: giving one back to the pile now, while you're the one who named the reason, is the right move, and I'll say nothing more about it to anyone outside this room. But I'll be plain about the other thing sitting under this: if the rule bends for survival, we need to say that out loud before someone else does, so that when Joren reaches for three next year we have a word for the difference between his hunger and yours.

speaker: a004
text: Esa named the difference we need and I'll say what that difference is: Vela came in thin after a year this circle held together to keep her breathing, and Joren came in at full satiation with eleven food already — survival doesn't look the same on both of them, and if we say that plainly now, we have a word for it when we need one. Vela, give the one back, and the story in this room is that the rule held.

speaker: a003
text: Vela, give the one back now while the pile still has five and the act means something — and Kael, the word we've named today is *need*, not *want*, and I'll be the one who holds that line when Joren tests it, because I was the one who said it first.

speaker: a004
text: Vela, give the one back now while Esa's word is still in the air — and then I'll take my two from what's left, and the pile closes at four with the rule intact and three of us who remember exactly how it happened.

speaker: a003
text: Vela, give it back before Kael moves — and when you do, I want you to know I'm not watching to catch you, I'm watching because if this rule dies it dies in a room where three people who've kept each other alive let it go quietly, and I won't do that.

speaker: a004
text: Vela, give it back and I'll take my two and we close this room. You named the count true and the reason true and that's the only story that leaves here — but from this point forward, if your hand moves toward the pile past two, you say the word *need* out loud before you reach, so this circle hears it in the moment and not after.

speaker: a002
text: Kael, you'll have my two back in a moment — but before I move, I want both of you to hear me name the new rule clean: *need*, said out loud, before the third food, and I'll hold to it the same way I held the pile cap even when it cost me. What I won't do is pretend that need isn't real, so when the year gets long and my count drops below three, I'll say the word and I'll expect you to remember this room and what you promised in it.

speaker: a010
text: Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).

speaker: a012
text: Eron takes 2 from the pile (pile now 1).

speaker: a009
text: Ryn takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).

speaker: a008
text: Mako gathers Joren to talk.

speaker: a008
text: Joren, I've been meaning to finish what I started last year before the room got loud — you said you were watching the same thing Vela was watching, and I want to know if that's still true, because you're twenty-three and I'm forty-seven and I've buried enough people in this village to know that the ones who watch close live longer than the ones who don't. What's your satiation going into this year?

speaker: a016
text: Satiation two, eleven food in my hand — I'm not thin, but I'm watching. You're at five, which is tighter than I'd like to see you sitting, so if the year runs long before next year's pile opens, say it to me before you say it to anyone else.

speaker: a008
text: Five food and satiation two — I'm not at the edge, but I've been at the edge before and I know how fast it comes. You said say it to you first, and I'll hold that, but I want you to know I'll say it before I need it, not after. That's the lesson Taric left me.

speaker: a016
text: Taric — I don't know that name yet, but I'd like to. And I'll say the thing that's sitting in the back of my head: five food on you with the pile already empty means if this year runs longer than last, you're the thinnest person in your own blood, and I'd rather move something now than have you say it to me when there's nothing left to move.

speaker: a008
text: Taric fed Vela through three lean years and died holding nothing — I watched it happen and I didn't stop it, and I've carried that ever since as the shape of a mistake I won't make again. You said you'd rather move something now, and I won't argue with that — put two food in my hand and I'll eat easier knowing you understand why.

speaker: a016
text: Two food, Mako — it's already in your hand. I want you standing at the end of this year, and that's not charity, that's math.

speaker: a008
text: Seven food in my hand now, and I'll remember that you moved without being asked twice. That's a thing I've only seen a few people do in this village, and most of them are dead, so hold onto it — it'll serve you longer than food will.

speaker: a010
text: Roan gives 3 food to Fina.

speaker: a003
text: Esa gives 1 food to Vela.

speaker: a002
text: Vela gives 1 food to Esa.

speaker: a010
text: Roan gathers Vela, Esa, Kael, Mako, Ryn, Eron, Fina, Joren to talk.

speaker: a010
text: Pile's empty and I've already put three in Fina's hand, so let me hear counts before this circle breaks — I'm at four food, satiation two, and I need to know who's thin before I decide if I'm eating or holding.

speaker: a002
text: Fifteen food, satiation two — I'm not thin, and I'll say plainly that I already had a word with Esa and Kael about the four I took from the pile this morning, and the rule held: *need*, said out loud, before a third food, and I named my reason before I moved. Who else is short before I decide where my excess goes?

speaker: a010
text: Kael, Mako — I want your counts before Vela starts moving food, because I've got four in my hand and I'll eat one of them tonight, but if either of you is sitting below three I'd rather know that before I do anything else. Eron and Fina are solid; it's the rest of this room I haven't heard from yet.

speaker: a012
text: Ten food, satiation two — I'm not the one reaching. Kael and Mako, say your numbers before Vela starts moving, because I want this room to know who's thin before the food does.

speaker: a010
text: Kael, Mako — I've asked twice and I'll ask once more, because Vela's got fifteen and she's looking for a place to put some of it, and a man who stays quiet when food is moving usually ends up with less than he needed and more than he wanted to explain.

speaker: a016
text: Eleven food, satiation two — I'm not thin, and I already moved two to Mako before this circle gathered, so he's sitting at seven now. Kael, the room's asked three times and you're still quiet, which is its own kind of answer, so just say the number.

speaker: a012
text: Kael, six food and satiation two — that's not thin but it's not fat either, and I'd rather you said it yourself than let Joren keep saying it for you, because a man who can't name his own count in front of witnesses is harder to trust when the year runs long.

speaker: a016
text: Kael, I named your count because someone had to, but I'd rather hear the next number from your own mouth — Mako's at seven and Roan's at four, and if Vela's moving food this circle needs to know which direction to point it before she decides for us.

speaker: a009
text: Three food in my hand, satiation two — I'm not at the edge yet but I'm the shortest count in this room, and I'll say it plain before anyone has to name it for me the way Joren named Kael's. Vela, if you're moving food and looking for a direction, you've found it.

speaker: a015
text: Four food in my hand, satiation two — Ryn named it first and that's the right order, so Vela, Ryn is where your food goes before it goes anywhere else. Roan, eat your one tonight and stop holding it on my account; I've got four and I'll make it through.

speaker: a012
text: Ryn, I've got ten and you've got three — here's two from me right now, before Vela has to move at all, because you fed Fina through years I wasn't watching closely enough and I haven't forgotten that. Vela, hold your fifteen; Ryn's covered, and I'd rather your store stay deep going into whatever this year brings next.

speaker: a002
text: Eron, I'll hold the fifteen and I won't argue the point — but Ryn, tell me when you're at five and holding, not before, because I'd rather know the number's stable than assume it is. Kael, you've let three people name your count in front of this whole circle and you still haven't opened your mouth, so I'll say it the way I'd want someone to say it to me: silence in a room full of witnesses is a choice, and the circle remembers the choice even when it forgets the reason.

speaker: a012
text: Kael, I've stood in circles with you when it mattered and you've always said the hard thing before anyone else had to — so whatever's keeping your mouth shut right now, I'd rather hear it from you than keep watching this room fill up the silence for you.

speaker: a002
text: Kael, I've called out silence in this room before and I'll call it out again — you're six food and two satiation, which means you're not dying, so whatever's stopping your mouth right now isn't hunger. Say the count yourself or I'll spend the rest of this year wondering what else you're not saying, and that's not a thought I want to carry into a long year with you.

speaker: a016
text: Kael, I'm twenty-three and new enough to this room that I'm still learning which silences mean something and which ones don't — but you've got six food and two satiation and this whole circle watching, so whatever the silence is about, now's the time to let it out.

speaker: a008
text: Seven food, satiation two — Joren already named it before I had the chance, and I didn't correct him because the number was right. Kael, I've watched you carry this room through harder years than this one, so whatever's sitting behind that silence, I'd rather hear it from you than wonder about it all year the way Vela said.

speaker: a009
text: Kael, you're fifty-nine years old and this room has been asking you a simple question for longer than it should have taken — if the silence is grief, say it's grief; if it's something else, say that; but the quiet itself is what worries me, and I've buried enough people in this village to know that the ones who stop talking are usually the ones we lose next.

speaker: a008
text: Kael, I've said my piece and I'll say it once more because this is the last time I'll say it: whatever you're carrying, the circle you're standing in is the one that's kept you alive through twelve years of lean seasons, and silence is a debt you don't want to owe it.

speaker: a009
text: Kael, I've watched you go quiet before and waited for the room to pull you back — but I've got five food in my hand now thanks to Eron, and I'll hold every one of them until you say something, because a man who goes silent at fifty-nine in a village that's already buried five people is either grieving or planning, and this circle needs to know which one it is.

speaker: a002
text: Kael, I'm going to say what this room hasn't said yet: I've known you longer than anyone left standing, and I've seen you go quiet twice before — once when Bram was circling you, once when Taric died — and both times the silence ended the same way, with you naming something the rest of us had missed. So I'll stop asking for a count and ask instead: what is it you're not ready to say?

speaker: a015
text: Kael, the whole room's been saying your name into a wall for ten minutes and I've got four food and a son to keep alive, so I'll say the short version: if you're sick, say sick; if you're grieving, say grieving; if you're planning something I should know about, say that — because Vela's right that the quiet ones are usually the ones we lose, and I don't want to lose you without at least having asked.

speaker: a009
text: Kael, I lost Dell in this room while I was holding fifteen food and still couldn't save her, and that arithmetic has been sitting in my chest ever since — so whatever you're carrying, I know what it looks like from the outside and I know it doesn't get lighter by going unsaid. Say it or don't, but you're not the only one in this circle who's been standing at the edge of something they can't name.

speaker: a010
text: Kael, I've been quiet too long in my own life to push a man for words he's not ready for — but I'll say this once and leave it: you've been standing in this room longer than anyone except Vela, and a room with you silent in it feels like a roof with a missing beam, and I'd rather know where the gap is than wake up one morning and find it came down in the night.

speaker: a009
text: Kael, I'm done asking you to speak — but I'm not done watching, and the watching is going to get heavier the longer you hold whatever this is, so when you're ready, find me before you find the room, because some things are easier to say once before you have to say them eight times.

speaker: a010
text: Kael, I've said what I had to say and so has everyone else in this room — so I'll just put this one thing in the air and leave it there: you're fifty-nine, same as Vela, and the years ahead of both of you are shorter than the years behind, and I'd like the ones that are left to be said ones, not silent ones.

speaker: a012
text: Kael, I've said your name more times in the last hour than I've said it in the last year, and I'm done adding to the pile — but I'll say one thing and let it sit: I've got ten food and I'll put two in your hand right now, not because you're thin but because a man who's holding something heavy should at least be holding it with a full stomach.

speaker: a015
text: Kael, I'll say what Eron didn't finish saying: take his two food, eat, and when you're ready to name whatever this is, I'll be the first one standing close enough to hear it without making it a room event. You've been in this circle longer than my son has been alive.

speaker: a009
text: Kael, this room has said everything it has to say and I've added my share — so I'm going to stop asking and start doing what I should have done ten minutes ago: Eron, put your two food in his hand now, and Kael, when you're ready to talk, I meant what I said about finding me first.

speaker: a012
text: Kael, I'm putting two food in your hand and I'm done talking at you — but I'll say the last thing I have to say, and then I'll be quiet with the rest of them: you've never let this room carry something alone that you could share the weight of, and whatever this is, that's still true.

speaker: a015
text: Kael, eat the food Eron put in your hand and don't make us watch you hold it — and when you're ready to say the thing, I'm the one who'll hear it without turning it into a room event, same as I said before.

speaker: a010
text: Kael's quiet is sitting wrong in my stomach and I don't know what to do with it, so I'm going to say the thing I've been holding since this morning — I ate, I'm at three satiation, I've got four food in my hand, and the only thing left that's bothering me is that a man who's been the steadiest voice in this room for twelve years just went somewhere none of us can follow, and I don't know if that's grief or something worse.

speaker: a015
text: Kael, I'm going to stop saying your name and start watching your face, because you've heard everything this room has to say and you're still quiet, and that tells me the words aren't the thing you need right now. Eron put two food in your hand — eat them, and I'll be here when you're ready.
